questions.q: Which real response header tells you exactly how many seconds to wait after hitting a 429?
options: anthropic-ratelimit-requests-reset
anthropic-ratelimit-tokens-limit
retry-after
anthropic-workspace-id
questions.explain: retry-after appears on a 429 response and gives the exact number of seconds to wait, removing the need to guess a backoff time.

questions.q: What does the anthropic-ratelimit-requests-remaining header tell you?
options: The total number of requests your organization has ever made
How many requests you have left before you'd get rate limited
The current server load percentage
The model's current version number
questions.explain: The -remaining header shows current headroom — how much capacity is left before you'd hit the limit.

questions.q: What algorithm does Anthropic's API use to enforce rate limits?
options: A token bucket, where capacity refills continuously rather than resetting on a fixed timer
A fixed daily quota that resets once every 24 hours
First-come-first-served with no limit at all
A lottery system that randomly rejects requests
questions.explain: Anthropic's documentation describes a token bucket algorithm: capacity is continuously replenished up to a maximum, rather than reset at fixed intervals.

questions.q: What is 'proactive throttling', as described in this lesson?
options: Waiting for a 429 error before taking any action
Disabling retries entirely
Slowing down your own request rate before you actually hit the limit, by watching -remaining headers
Always waiting exactly 60 seconds between every request
questions.explain: Proactive throttling means easing off based on the -remaining headers before a 429 ever happens, rather than only reacting after the fact.

questions.q: Why is reading retry-after better than always guessing a fixed backoff time (like Lesson 18's 1s/2s/4s)?
options: retry-after is always exactly 1 second
It isn't better — guessing is always just as accurate
retry-after gives the API's own precise, real wait time instead of an arbitrary guess
retry-after disables rate limiting entirely
questions.explain: When present, retry-after is the API telling you exactly how long to wait — more accurate than an arbitrary fixed backoff schedule.
